earnings.title: Snap-on Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
highlights: Sales of $1,183.7 million and diluted EPS of $4.64 for the third quarter of 2026;

Operating earnings before financial services for the quarter of $248.1 million, or 21.0% of net sales, compared to $278.5 million, or 23.4% of net sales, last year, which included a benefit of $22.0 million, or 190 basis points, from the settlement of a legal matter (the “legal settlement”).

Consolidated operating earnings for the quarter of $316.4 million, or 24.7% of revenues (net sales plus financial services revenue), compared to $347.4 million, or 26.9% of revenues, in 2025, which included a benefit of $22.0 million, or 170 basis points, from the legal settlement.
Financial services revenue in the quarter of $98.6 million compared to $101.1 million in 2025; financial services operating earnings of $68.3 million compared to $68.9 million last year.

Commercial & Industrial Group segment sales of $404.3 million in the quarter compared to $367.7 million last year, reflecting a $27.0 million, or 7.4%, organic gain and $10.0 million of acquisition-related sales, partially offset by $0.4 million of unfavorable foreign currency translation.

quotes.text: Our third quarter was mixed with varied outcomes among our business groups.
quotes.by: Nick Pinchuk, Snap-on chairman and chief executive officer

outlook: Snap-on currently anticipates that its full-year 2026 effective income tax rate will approximate 22%.

items.heading: The sales of many of our products are dependent on the health of the vehicle repair market and the changing requirements of vehicle repair.
The performance of Snap-on’s mobile tool distribution business depends on the success of its franchisees.
The inability to continue to introduce new products that respond to customer needs and achieve market acceptance could result in lower revenues and reduced profitability.
Failure to adequately protect intellectual property, or claims of infringement, could adversely affect our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
Foreign operations are subject to political, economic, trade and other risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
Risks associated with the disruption of manufacturing operations could adversely affect our profitability or competitive position.
